indicators.label: Is climate getting worse here?
indicators.description: For each district, the weighted share of the Rama Rao indicators that end up at least 10% worse than the district's own 1985–2014 mean. An absolute measure: it can be compared across scenarios. More rain counts as better only where baseline rainfall is below 1,500 mm; unusually hot and cold days and drought have weight 0 because the ensemble-mean data cannot represent them.

indicators.label: Where should we act first?
indicators.description: Districts ranked against each other within the selected scenario: each indicator ranks districts from least to most adverse change, and the weighted average rank (0–100) is split into fifths. A relative measure: it shows where hazard is highest, not whether climate is getting worse.

indicators.label: Future hazard index
indicators.description: Aggregate future climate hazard for agriculture, following Rama Rao et al. (2020): the 15 indicators below, each as a change from 1985–2014, normalised with sign kept and combined with the Atlas Table 5c weights. Positive = climate becoming less favourable, negative = more favourable. Shown by district for a future period.

indicators.label: Annual rainfall
indicators.description: Total precipitation over the year (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: June rainfall
indicators.description: Total rainfall in June, the month of monsoon onset and kharif sowing (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: July rainfall
indicators.description: Total rainfall in July, the main crop-establishment month (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Rainy days (≥ 2.5 mm)
indicators.description: Days per year with at least 2.5 mm of rain (IMD rainy-day definition). Note: averaging 14 models gives light rain on more days than any single model, so absolute counts run high; the change is what enters the index.

indicators.label: Maximum temperature
indicators.description: Average of daily maximum temperatures over the year (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Minimum temperature
indicators.description: Average of daily minimum temperatures over the year (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Unusually hot days (Mar–May)
indicators.description: Days in March–May when maximum temperature is at least 2 standard deviations above the 1985–2014 normal for that date. The Atlas uses +4 °C; the threshold is scaled because the ensemble-mean data varies far less from day to day than real weather.

indicators.label: Unusually cold days (Dec–Feb)
indicators.description: Days in December–February when minimum temperature is at least 2 standard deviations below the 1985–2014 normal for that date. The Atlas uses −4 °C; the threshold is scaled for the same reason as hot days.

indicators.label: Frost days
indicators.description: Days per year when the minimum temperature falls below 0°C. Frost damages rabi crops such as mustard, chickpea and potato; mostly relevant in the hills.

indicators.label: Drought proneness (proxy: SPI-3 drought frequency)
indicators.description: Proxy for the Atlas's drought proneness (severe and moderate drought, weighted 2:1): percentage of months with 3-month Standardised Precipitation Index below −1. The Atlas's rainfall-deficit definition gives near-zero droughts on ensemble-mean data, while SPI rescales by the data's own variability.

indicators.label: Dry-spell score (Jun–Oct, ≥ 14 days)
indicators.description: Atlas dry-spell score: for each June–October dry spell (rain < 2.5 mm) of 14 days or more, add exp(length/14 − 1), with length capped at 42 days. Longer spells score much more.

indicators.label: 99th-percentile daily rainfall
indicators.description: Rainfall on the wettest 1% of days in a year (annual 99th percentile, averaged over years). Indicates the intensity of extreme rain.

indicators.label: Events with > 100 mm in 3 days
indicators.description: Number of distinct events per year in which rainfall over 3 consecutive days exceeds 100 mm — a flood and crop-damage hazard (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Max 1-day rain as % of annual normal
indicators.description: Wettest single day of the year as a percentage of the 1985–2014 annual normal rainfall. Higher values mean rain is concentrated in fewer, heavier events.

indicators.label: Max 3-day rain as % of annual normal
indicators.description: Wettest 3-day period of the year as a percentage of the 1985–2014 annual normal rainfall.

indicators.label: Heat stress days (Tmax > 35°C)
indicators.description: Days per year when the daily maximum temperature exceeds 35°C. Above this, many crops (e.g. wheat, rice at flowering) suffer heat stress and outdoor work becomes harder.

indicators.label: Heat stress days (Tmax > 40°C)
indicators.description: Days per year when the daily maximum temperature exceeds 40°C — severe heat for crops, livestock and people.

indicators.label: Tropical nights (Tmin > 25°C)
indicators.description: Nights per year when the minimum temperature stays above 25°C. Warm nights raise crop respiration losses and prevent livestock and people from recovering from daytime heat.

indicators.label: Heatwave days (≥ 3 consecutive days > 40°C)
indicators.description: Days per year that fall in a spell of 3 or more consecutive days with maximum temperature above 40°C.

indicators.label: Extreme heat days (Tmax > 45°C)
indicators.description: Days per year with maximum temperature above 45°C — extreme heat associated with heat-related deaths and crop failure.

indicators.label: Cooling degree days (base 18°C)
indicators.description: Cooling degree days: the yearly sum of how far daily mean temperature exceeds 18°C. A measure of cumulative heat load and cooling demand.

indicators.label: Annual mean temperature
indicators.description: Average daily mean temperature over the year (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Diurnal temperature range
indicators.description: Diurnal temperature range: average difference between daily maximum and minimum temperature.

indicators.label: Summer mean temperature (Apr–Jun)
indicators.description: Average daily mean temperature, computed as (Tmax + Tmin) / 2, over April–June, the hottest pre-monsoon months (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Heating degree days (base 18°C)
indicators.description: Heating degree days: the yearly sum of how far daily mean temperature falls below 18°C. A measure of cold load.

indicators.label: Max 1-day precipitation
indicators.description: Wettest single day of the year: the highest one-day rainfall total, averaged over years. Indicates flash-flood and waterlogging risk.

indicators.label: Max 5-day precipitation
indicators.description: Wettest 5-day period of the year: the highest 5-day rainfall total, averaged over years (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Rain share from very wet days (> 95th pct)
indicators.description: Share of annual rainfall that falls on very wet days (days above the 95th percentile of the 1985–2014 baseline). Higher values mean rain is more concentrated in intense events.

indicators.label: Rain share from extremely wet days (> 99th pct)
indicators.description: Share of annual rainfall that falls on extremely wet days (days above the 99th percentile of the 1985–2014 baseline).

indicators.label: Wet days (R ≥ 1 mm)
indicators.description: Wet days per year (daily rainfall of at least 1 mm). Closest available match to Rama Rao's rainy days (≥ 2.5 mm).

indicators.label: Heavy rain days (R ≥ 10 mm)
indicators.description: Days per year with at least 10 mm of rain.

indicators.label: Very heavy rain days (R ≥ 20 mm)
indicators.description: Days per year with at least 20 mm of rain.

indicators.label: Kharif season precipitation (Jun–Sep)
indicators.description: Total rainfall during the kharif (south-west monsoon) season, June–September.

indicators.label: Monsoon onset day
indicators.description: Estimated day of year when the monsoon sets in. Later onset delays kharif sowing.

indicators.label: Max 3-day precipitation
indicators.description: Wettest 3-day period of the year: the highest 3-day rainfall total, averaged over years.

indicators.label: Consecutive dry days
indicators.description: Consecutive dry days: the longest run of days with less than 1 mm of rain each year. A measure of dry-spell length (Rama Rao indicator).

indicators.label: Consecutive wet days
indicators.description: Consecutive wet days: the longest run of days with at least 1 mm of rain each year.

indicators.label: SPEI-3 drought frequency (SPEI < −1)
indicators.description: Percentage of months in moderate or worse drought on the 3-month Standardised Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (below −1). Unlike SPI, it also counts the drying effect of higher temperatures.

indicators.label: Growing degree days (base 10°C)
indicators.description: Growing degree days above 10°C: the yearly sum of daily mean temperature above 10°C. Measures heat available for crop growth; more GDD speeds crop development.

indicators.label: Killing degree days (base 38°C)
indicators.description: Killing degree days: the yearly sum of how far daily temperature exceeds 38°C. Heat above this threshold damages most crops.

indicators.label: Growing season length
indicators.description: Growing season length: days per year between the first and last spells warm enough for plant growth (mean temperature above 5°C). Saturates at 365 across most of India.

indicators.label: Rabi season max temperature (Nov–Mar)
indicators.description: Average daily maximum temperature in the rabi season (November–March). Warmer rabi seasons, especially terminal heat, cut wheat yields.

indicators.label: Extreme temperature range
indicators.description: Extreme temperature range: the difference between the year's highest maximum and lowest minimum temperature.
